sample.description: Three baskets from yfinance daily data: G10 FX 9 pairs vs USD (EURUSD=X, GBPUSD=X, USDJPY=X, USDCHF=X, USDCAD=X, AUDUSD=X, NZDUSD=X, USDSEK=X, USDNOK=X), 5 iShares multifactor ETFs on LSE (IFSU.L, IUSZ.L, IUVL.L, IUMO.L, IUQA.L), US Treasuries 4 yield indices ^IRX/^FVX/^TNX/^TYX (3M/5Y/10Y/30Y). Primary X_t = demeaned log price levels (FX/ETF) and demeaned yield levels (TSY) – chosen to produce smooth slow components matching paper figures; returns-based X_t reported as robustness. Windows: G10 2006-01-01–2010-12-31 fit (1182 bars) 2011-01-01–2025-06-30 OOS (3770 bars), ETF 2021-01-01–2022-12-31 fit (503) 2023-01-01–2025-06-30 OOS (629), TSY 1994-01-01–1998-12-31 fit (1252) 1999-01-01–2025-06-30 OOS (6655). Linear tICA k=1: generalized eigenvalue C_T w=lambda C0 w, C0=X^T X/N, C_T symmetrized lag-1 autocov, T=1d, scipy.linalg.eigh with 1e-10 ridge, timescales t=-2T/(lambda-1). Tail tICA k=4: FastICA fixed-point on whitened Z=X C0^{-1/2}, parallel symmetric orthogonalization, seed 0, tol 1e-6.
sample.cannot_count: Paper prints no observation count, data vendor, or exact G10/Treasury instrument list, so missing/extra vs paper's vendor data cannot be counted; counts here reflect public yfinance daily coverage for standard proxies overlapping paper windows.
sample.substitutions: G10: yfinance daily spot closes for 9 G10 pairs vs USD (paper G10 list unspecified; using standard 9 USD-crosses covering G10 ex-USD). ETF: LSE listings .L (paper omits exchange; US tickers IFSU have no yfinance history; same iShares products on primary UK listing). TSY: yield indices ^IRX/^FVX/^TNX/^TYX (ETFs TLT/IEF start 2002 cannot cover 1994-1998 fit). X_t demeaned log price levels (FX/ETF) and yield levels (TSY) as primary – paper says prices or returns without per-basket choice; returns reported as robustness. Lag T=1d, sample mean covariance, ridge 1e-10, symmetric whitening, single random init FastICA (paper lag, estimator, init/tol not stated).

notes: Paper leaves open: G10 composition, Treasury maturities/instruments, data vendor/source, frequency (we use daily closes), price vs return definition (we use levels as primary because it yields smooth slow components matching figures; returns alternative gives lambdas ~0.1 IS and ~0 OOS with no persistence – reported as _returns_ robustness), demeaning (we demean per window to enforce zero-mean), lag T and discretization of dX_t (we use T=1 trading day, symmetrized C_T=1/2 E[X_{t+T}^T X_t+X_t^T X_{t+T}]), covariance expectation estimator (we use sample mean without shrinkage), FastICA init/tol/restarts (we use seed 0, tol 1e-6, parallel orth, single restart; increasing k beyond 4 not tested beyond k=4). Deviations: fit/OOS split at year-end (2010/2011, 2022/2023, 1998/1999) to avoid overlap vs paper inclusive 2010-2025 etc – windows within paper ranges. Treasuries OOS to 2025-06-30 (latest yfinance). Weights kept C0-normalized (w^T C0 w=1) for lambda; paper figures rescale to unit gross exposure (sum|w|=1) which cancels in autocorr. Paper prints no numeric table, test statistic, SE or p-value – main conclusion is visual robustness of timescale at IS/OOS transition and reversion after shocks, with orthogonality decaying as expected. We quantify persistence via slowest-component lambda/timescale IS vs OOS, correlation of top-m lambdas, mean absolute lambda difference, and Frobenius deviation of W C0 W^T from identity OOS. All numbers recomputed from public data; no paper-reported number copied. Tail lambdas (=E[Y^{2k-1} Y_{t+T}]) numerically unstable in whitened space due to outlier amplification (Y^7) – values range 1e0 to 1e18, outside [-1,1] – reported as computed without normalization; paper does not print tail eigenvalues either.
